ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: The figure is equilateral triangle ABC, with A and B at the two ends of the base and C at the vertex. Inside the triangle there are several dividing lines parallel to the three sides, dividing each side into three equal parts and forming a standard triangular grid whose side length is one third of the original triangle. There are three gray shaded parts: a rhombus region in the upper middle, a quadrilateral region in the lower left, and a quadrilateral region in the lower right. Reasoning: Since the three sides of the triangle are all trisected and connected with parallel lines, the whole large equilateral triangle can be regarded as being composed of 9 congruent smallest equilateral triangles. The upper gray rhombus in the figure is composed of 2 smallest triangles, the lower-left gray quadrilateral is composed of 2 smallest triangles, and the lower-right gray quadrilateral is also composed of 2 smallest triangles, so the gray part covers 6 smallest triangles in total. The area of the large triangle is 9, so the area of each smallest triangle is 9/9=1. The gray area is 6×1=6.

Thus the grey region covers 6 congruent smallest equilateral triangles out of the 9 congruent smallest triangles in the whole triangle. From the text, the total area is 9, so each smallest triangle has area 1. Therefore the grey area is 6.

method.method_draft: First read the diagram by focusing on the unshaded complement rather than the shaded pieces. The image shows three unshaded small equilateral triangles: one near the left side, one inverted near the bottom center, and one near the right side. Because the dividing lines are parallel to the sides and hit the sides at thirds, each of these unshaded triangles has side length one-third of the side of ABC. From the text, area(ABC) = 9. By similarity, each unshaded triangle has area 9 times (1/3)^2 = 1. The unshaded area is 3, so the grey area is 9 - 3 = 6.
